strings.d1.s0.name: Senso-ji
strings.d1.s0.tips: Tokyo's oldest temple. See the Kaminarimon lantern, and come at 08:00 when Nakamise is empty. Draw an omikuji fortune.
strings.d1.s1.name: Nakamise Dori
strings.d1.s1.tips: Shops lining the temple approach. Try ningyo-yaki (small sponge cakes) and senbei (rice crackers).
strings.d1.s2.name: Asakusa Kappabashi
strings.d1.s2.tips: Kitchenware street. Look for Japanese knives and plastic food models.
strings.d1.s3.name: Asakusa Unatoto
strings.d1.s3.tips: Cheap unagi (eel) donburi. The queue is short.
strings.d1.s4.name: Tokyo Skytree
strings.d1.s4.tips: 634 m tall. Book Tembo Deck tickets online, go in the afternoon for clear skies, and walk over the Sumida River.
strings.d1.b0.name: Asakusa Imahan
strings.d1.b0.tips: Sukiyaki since 1895. Go for the special lunch.
strings.d1.b1.name: Sumida River Cruise
strings.d1.b1.tips: Water bus from Asakusa to Odaiba. Take it instead of Skytree.
strings.d2.s0.name: Meiji Jingu
strings.d2.s0.tips: Shinto shrine in the forest. See the sake barrels. It is calm in the morning, and wedding processions pass on weekends.
strings.d2.s1.name: Takeshita Street
strings.d2.s1.tips: Harajuku youth fashion. Crepe stalls line the street, and it gets packed after 11:00.
strings.d2.s2.name: Omotesando
strings.d2.s2.tips: Tokyo's Champs-Élysées. Come for the architecture and the mirrored entrance of Tokyu Plaza.
strings.d2.s3.name: Afuri Ramen Harajuku
strings.d2.s3.tips: Yuzu shio ramen. Order from the ticket machine.
strings.d2.s4.name: Shibuya Sky
strings.d2.s4.tips: Open-air terrace above the Shibuya Scramble. Book the sunset slot online weeks ahead, and watch the crossing from above.
strings.d2.b0.name: Ichiran Shibuya
strings.d2.b0.tips: Tonkotsu ramen in single-person booths. Open 24 hours.
strings.d2.b1.name: Yoyogi Park
strings.d2.b1.tips: Park next to Meiji Jingu. Rockabilly dancers perform on weekends.
strings.d3.s0.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
strings.d3.s0.tips: Morning stalls serve tamago (sweet omelette), uni and tuna. Go before 10:00 and eat standing up.
strings.d3.s1.name: Hamarikyu Gardens
strings.d3.s1.tips: Edo-period garden among the skyscrapers. Have matcha in the tea house.
strings.d3.s2.name: Ginza Chuo Dori
strings.d3.s2.tips: Closed to traffic on weekends. Visit the Itoya stationery store and the 12-floor Uniqlo.
strings.d3.s3.name: Ginza Kagari Ramen
strings.d3.s3.tips: Chicken paitan ramen. It is a small counter, so expect a queue.
strings.d3.s4.name: teamLab Planets
strings.d3.s4.tips: Digital art museum where you wade through water. Book online weeks ahead and wear shorts (the water is knee-deep).
strings.d3.b0.name: Sushi Dai Toyosu
strings.d3.b0.tips: Legendary sushi at Toyosu Market. The queue starts at 05:00.
strings.d3.b1.name: Ginza Six Rooftop Garden
strings.d3.b1.tips: Shopping mall rooftop. Go here if you have no teamLab ticket.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
strings.d4.s0.tips: Free observation deck on the 45th floor. Mount Fuji is visible in clear weather.
strings.d4.s1.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
strings.d4.s1.tips: Japanese, English and French gardens. Best in sakura and momiji (autumn leaf) season.
strings.d4.s2.name: Fuunji Shinjuku
strings.d4.s2.tips: Tsukemen (dipping ramen) legend. Expect a 20-minute queue.
strings.d4.s3.name: Yanaka Ginza
strings.d4.s3.tips: Old Tokyo (shitamachi) shopping street. Look for cats and menchi katsu (fried minced meat cutlet), and visit Yanaka Cemetery.
strings.d4.s4.name: Omoide Yokocho
strings.d4.s4.tips: Izakaya alley in Shinjuku. Yakitori and beer, nicknamed 'Piss Alley'.
strings.d4.b0.name: Golden Gai
strings.d4.b0.tips: Neighbourhood of tiny bars. Ask about the cover charge.
strings.d4.b1.name: Nezu Shrine
strings.d4.b1.tips: Tunnel of red torii gates near Yanaka. Azaleas bloom in April.
strings.d5.s0.name: Ueno Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: Park of museums. It is the heart of Tokyo in sakura season.
strings.d5.s1.name: Tokyo National Museum
strings.d5.s1.tips: Japan's largest museum. See samurai armour and ukiyo-e prints.
strings.d5.s2.name: Ameyoko Market
strings.d5.s2.tips: Market beneath the Ueno tracks. Street food and dried fruit.
strings.d5.s3.name: Akihabara Electric Town
strings.d5.s3.tips: Electronics, anime and retro games. Try Yodobashi and Super Potato.
strings.d5.s4.name: Odaiba Seaside Park
strings.d5.s4.tips: Artificial island reached by the Yurikamome line. Watch sunset at Rainbow Bridge and see the giant Gundam.
strings.d5.b0.name: Kanda Matsuya Soba
strings.d5.b1.name: Ueno Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: Pandas. Go instead of the museum.
strings.d6.s0.name: Kotoku-in Great Buddha
strings.d6.s0.tips: One hour from Tokyo. A 13 m bronze Buddha you can step inside.
strings.d6.s1.name: Hase-dera
strings.d6.s1.tips: Temple with a hydrangea garden. Views over Kamakura's coast.
strings.d6.s2.name: Komachi Dori
strings.d6.s2.tips: Kamakura's food street. Try shirasu (baby fish) donburi.
strings.d6.s3.name: Yuigahama Beach
strings.d6.s3.tips: Kamakura's beach. Swimming and beach cafes in summer.
strings.d6.s4.name: Enoshima Island
strings.d6.s4.tips: Reach the island by Enoden train. Sunset and the silhouette of Mount Fuji.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kamakura Bowls Cafe
strings.d6.b1.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu
strings.d7.theme: Tokyo Station and Imperial Palace: a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
strings.d7.s0.tips: Gardens of the former Edo castle. Free entry, closed on Mondays and Fridays.
strings.d7.s1.name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi
strings.d7.s1.tips: Red-brick station from 1914. Visit Character Street and pick up an ekiben (station bento).
strings.d7.s2.name: Rokurinsha Tokyo Station
strings.d7.s2.tips: Tsukemen on Ramen Street. A farewell lunch.
strings.d7.s3.name: Tokyo Character Street
strings.d7.s3.tips: Souvenirs. Look for Kit Kat flavours and Tokyo Banana.
strings.d7.s4.name: Narita Express / Keisei
strings.d7.s4.tips: Narita takes 1 hour, Haneda 30 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Kitchen Street Tokyo Station
strings.d7.b1.name: Nihonbashi Bridge
strings.d7.b1.tips: Japan's kilometre zero. Coredo shopping mall.
strings.note0: Every train accepts a Suica card, and Google Maps is flawless for train times. A JR Pass is unnecessary within Tokyo; for Nikko, get the Tobu pass.
strings.note1: Summer brings 33°C heat and humidity, plus festivals and fireworks (hanabi) in July and August. Go out early in the morning and choose indoor venues in the afternoon.
strings.note2: Cash still matters, especially at small ramen shops. 7-Eleven ATMs accept foreign cards. There is no tipping.
strings.note3: Be quiet in temples and do not take photos inside. Do not talk on the phone on the metro, and do not eat while walking.
strings.note4: Book Shibuya Sky and teamLab tickets weeks ahead. Visit Tsukiji before 10:00.
strings.note5: Ramen costs 1,000-1,500 JPY, a konbini (convenience store) breakfast 500 JPY, and a sushi counter 3,000+.
strings.transit.name: Suica / Welcome Suica
strings.transit.why_chosen: Works on JR, metro, buses and at konbini (convenience stores), and can be added to your phone
